references.text: Jesus' promise that prayers in his name will be answered is directly linked to his claim that the disciples should do his works and even greater works, since both are made possible through his departure to the Father.
The condition for the disciples being able to perform Jesus' works is that they remain in him and his words, just as the answer to prayer in John 14:13 is conditioned on asking in his name.
Jesus' prayer for all future believers emphasizes that they should believe in him, so that they may continue his work and show the world that the Father has sent him.
The first chapter of Acts confirms that the disciples are to receive power to be Jesus' witnesses, which is the practical fulfillment of doing his works and even greater works.
Paul and Barnabas perform signs and wonders, which is a concrete fulfillment of the promise that the disciples should do Jesus' works and even greater works.
